items.text:
Sol.154.(c) Flushed having a reddish or rosy color, often due to excitement, heat, or embarrassment. Sallow  having  a  pale,  yellowish  skin tone, indicating sickness or tiredness. Pallid  very pale, often suggesting poor health or lack of vitality. Livid  extremely angry or having a dark, bluish discoloration due to bruising. Paled became lighter or lost color, often from fear, shock, or illness.
Sol.155.(a)  Enemies  a  person  who  is actively  opposed  or  hostile  to  someone or something. Allies -supporters or partners  who cooperate for a common purpose. Buddies close friends or companions. Scholars learned individuals or academics. Fellows -members of a group or community sharing similar interests.
Sol.156.(b)  Repulse  to  drive  back  or cause strong dislike. Entice  to  attract  or  tempt  by  offering pleasure or advantage. Allure to attract or charm. Invite -to  ask  someone  to  come  or participate. Tangle to twist together in a confusing mass.

items.text:
Sol.169.(a) Serious -solemn or thoughtful in character or manner. Risible - provoking laughter through being ludicrous. Curious -eager to know or learn something. Droll -  curious  or  unusual  in  a  way  that provokes dry amusement. Giddy - feeling silly, happy, and excited.
Sol.170.(c) Fertile -capable of producing abundant vegetation or crops. Barren -unable to produce any vegetation or crops. Sterile not able to reproduce. Infertile not able to conceive children or young. Unfruitful not yielding fruit or success.
Sol.171.(c)  Entry  a  place  for  entering, such as a door, gate, etc. Exit -a way  out, especially from a building or a large enclosed space. House a building for human habitation. Road  a  wide  way  leading  from  one place to another, typically paved. Ceremony a formal event performed on a special occasion.
Sol.172.(d)  Manual  done  by  hand,  not by machines. Mechanical operated by machinery. Surrogate  a substitute, especially for a person. Automatised -made to operate automatically. Yielding  giving  way  under  pressure  or influence.
